original_question: Is the geodesic flow of a metric of non-positive curvature on a closed surface of genus ≥ 2 ergodic with respect to the Liouville measure?
target_in_paper: Question 6.1.1 in §6.1 (“Ergodicity of geodesic flows”). Your draft is already essentially the paper’s official formulation. ([users.fmi.uni-jena.de](https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~matveev/Datei/problem_list_submitted.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures all of the core content of the paper’s official open problem: it asks about the geodesic flow, for a metric of non-positive curvature, on a closed surface of genus at least 2, and asks whether that flow is ergodic with respect to the Liouville measure. This is almost verbatim Question 6.1.1. ([users.fmi.uni-jena.de](https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~matveev/Datei/problem_list_submitted.pdf))
missing_details: It should explicitly identify the object as a smooth Riemannian metric g on a closed surface M; that is the ambient setup of the paper. ([users.fmi.uni-jena.de](https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~matveev/Datei/problem_list_submitted.pdf))

It is better to state that the geodesic flow acts on the unit tangent bundle SM; §1 defines SM and φ^t as the unit tangent bundle and geodesic flow attached to the metric. ([users.fmi.uni-jena.de](https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~matveev/Datei/problem_list_submitted.pdf))

To make “non-positive curvature” stand alone, one should spell out that the Gaussian curvature satisfies K_g ≤ 0 everywhere on M. The nearby §6.1–§6.2 discussion is precisely about geodesics through negative-curvature points versus geodesics along which the Gaussian curvature is identically zero. ([users.fmi.uni-jena.de](https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~matveev/Datei/problem_list_submitted.pdf))
It helps to specify that the Liouville measure is the natural Liouville measure induced by g on SM. ([users.fmi.uni-jena.de](https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~matveev/Datei/problem_list_submitted.pdf))

The nearby context worth retaining is that the unresolved obstruction is the invariant set of vectors tangent to zero-curvature geodesics, and §6.2.1 records the sharper related question of whether a non-closed such geodesic can exist. ([users.fmi.uni-jena.de](https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~matveev/Datei/problem_list_submitted.pdf))
refined_question: Let (M,g) be a closed C∞ Riemannian surface of genus at least 2 whose Gaussian curvature satisfies K_g ≤ 0 everywhere. Is the geodesic flow φ^t on the unit tangent bundle SM ergodic with respect to the Liouville measure induced by g? ([users.fmi.uni-jena.de](https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~matveev/Datei/problem_list_submitted.pdf))
justification: The nearest official formulation in arXiv:1308.5417 is exactly Question 6.1.1 in §6.1. The paragraph immediately following it explains the paper’s intended scope: ergodicity is already known on the set of geodesics passing through points where the curvature is negative, and the unresolved issue is whether the complementary invariant set of vectors tangent to zero-curvature geodesics must have measure zero. Section 6.2 then gives the closest sharper neighboring question—whether there exists a non-closed geodesic along which the Gaussian curvature is everywhere zero—and states that a negative answer there would imply a positive answer to Question 6.1.1. That is why the refined question should stay narrowly focused on the Liouville-ergodicity problem for closed genus-at-least-2 surfaces of non-positive curvature, while making the ambient objects and notation explicit. ([users.fmi.uni-jena.de](https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~matveev/Datei/problem_list_submitted.pdf))
